mainTopic: Holy animals blemished before or after their הקדש: their status after פדיון, and the גמרא's inferences about the state before פדיון
overview: This amud opens with a משנה comparing two kinds of blemished holy animals. If an animal had a permanent מום before it was made הקדש, only its money value was holy. Once redeemed, it becomes fully חולין, except for בכור and מעשר. If the הקדש came first, or the מום was only temporary at the time, the animal's body was holy. It keeps much of that holiness even after פדיון. The גמרא then reads the משנה closely. It infers that before פדיון, even קדושת דמים exempts an animal from בכורה and מתנות. It also suggests the ban on shearing and work before פדיון supports רבי אליעזר about בדק הבית animals, but rejects that proof. The ban might be only a decree for animals of the מזבח, made to prevent confusion. Finally, the גמרא works out that the permitted offspring were conceived before פדיון and born after it. So offspring born before פדיון are forbidden, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blemish before consecration: once redeemed, the animal is fully ordinary
steps.stepSummary: Holy animals that had a permanent מום before they were made הקדש become fully חולין after פדיון. Their offspring can be a בכור, they owe the מתנות, they may be shorn and worked, and their young and milk are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any holy animals that had a permanent blemish before they were consecrated, and were then redeemed, are obligated in the firstborn law and in the priestly gifts. They become fully ordinary, so they may be shorn and used for work. Their offspring and their milk are permitted after redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the first case: an animal that was already permanently blemished when someone made it הקדש. It lists the ways such an animal, once redeemed, is treated like any ordinary animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanently blemished animal can never go on the מזבח, so the הקדש only grabbed its money value, not the animal's body. That is why פדיון fully releases it. It becomes subject to בכורה and מתנות like any חולין animal, and it may even be shorn and worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish that disqualifies an animal from the altar
Consecration; making something holy property
They were redeemed (their holiness moved onto money)
The firstborn law: the animal's firstborn male goes to the כהן
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, jaw, and maw
To be shorn and to be worked

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with ordinary פסולי המוקדשין. Normally, a redeemed holy animal still may not be shorn or worked. This first case is special because the holiness never sat on the animal's body.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
phrases.english: MISHNA: All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish came before their consecration
and they were redeemed, are obligated in the firstborn law and in the gifts,
phrases.notes: This means their future firstborn counts as a בכור, and when they are slaughtered the כהן gets his gifts.

phrases.english: and they go out to ordinary status, to be shorn and to be worked,
and their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a permanent מום came before the הקדש, the animal becomes fully חולין after פדיון. It is obligated in בכורה and מתנות, may be shorn and worked, and its young and milk are permitted.

steps.title: More leniencies for the blemished-first animal, with בכור and מעשר as exceptions
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering such an animal outside the מקדש carries no penalty. It cannot create a תמורה. If it died, it may still be redeemed. None of this applies to בכור and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who slaughters them outside the Temple is exempt. They do not make a substitute animal holy. If they died, they may be redeemed. This is true of all of them except the firstborn and the animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing leniencies for the first case, an animal blemished before it was made הקדש. It ends by pointing out two kinds of animals where these leniencies do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because only the animal's value was holy, slaughtering it outside is not שחוטי חוץ. Its holiness is also too weak to create a תמורה. A dead animal is normally buried, but this one can be redeemed and its body used. בכור and מעשר are different: their holiness comes by itself, even on a blemished animal, so they keep full holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters a holy animal outside the Temple courtyard, normally punished with כרת
Swapping an ordinary animal for a holy one, which makes the new animal holy too
A firstborn male animal
The animal tithe, every tenth animal

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main contrast of the משנה. בכור and מעשר stand apart from other קדשים because their holiness takes hold even on a blemished animal.

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt,
phrases.notes: Outside means outside the Temple courtyard. He is exempt from the כרת that normally comes with this.

phrases.english: and they do not make a substitute,
phrases.notes: If someone tries to swap another animal for this one, the other animal does not become holy.

phrases.english: and if they died, they may be redeemed,
except for the firstborn and the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of laws for the first case and adds the exception of בכור and מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal blemished before its הקדש carries no שחוטי חוץ liability, makes no תמורה, and may be redeemed after death. בכור and מעשר are excluded.

steps.title: Consecration before the blemish: the animal does not become fully ordinary
steps.stepSummary: Now the second case. If the הקדש came first, or the animal had only a temporary מום at the time and later got a permanent one, then after פדיון it is exempt from בכורה and מתנות. It also may not be shorn or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all animals whose consecration came before their blemish, or that had a temporary blemish before their consecration and afterward developed a permanent blemish, and were then redeemed, are exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts. They do not go out to ordinary status to be shorn and to be worked.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the opposite case: an animal that became holy while it was still fit for the מזבח, or fit except for a temporary מום. It starts showing how the rules flip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the holiness took hold of the animal's body itself (קדושת הגוף). פדיון cannot fully erase that. So the animal does not count as plain חולין for בכורה and מתנות, and it stays forbidden for shearing and work. Notice that a temporary מום counts like no מום at all, because the animal could have healed and been brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that can heal
Exempt
And afterward

steps.confusionAlert: Being exempt from בכורה here is not a leniency. It shows the animal still keeps some holiness, so the laws for ordinary animals don't apply to it.

phrases.english: And all whose consecration came before their blemish,
or a temporary blemish came before their consecration,
phrases.notes: The words 'came before' carry over from the line above: the animal had only a temporary blemish when it was made holy.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד לָהֶן מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן וְנִפְדּוּ —
phrases.english: and afterward a permanent blemish developed in them, after their consecration, and they were redeemed,
they are exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts,
and they do not go out to ordinary status to be shorn and to be worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite case to Step 1 and reverses each law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the הקדש came first, or there was only a temporary מום at the time, the redeemed animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות and may not be shorn or worked.

steps.title: The consecrated-first animal: offspring and milk forbidden, liability outside, תמורה, burial
steps.stepSummary: For the second case, the animal's young and milk stay forbidden after פדיון. Slaughtering it outside brings liability. It does create a תמורה. If it died, it must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption. One who slaughters them outside the Temple is liable. They do make a substitute holy. If they died, they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the second case. Point by point, it reverses each leniency from Steps 1–2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each rule mirrors the first case and shows the body itself is still holy. The young and milk are forbidden, שחיטת חוץ brings liability, a swap creates a holy תמורה, and a dead animal cannot be redeemed and so must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring and their milk
Liable (here, to כרת)
They must be buried

steps.whatToRemember: The key question is which came first, the הקדש or the permanent מום. If the מום came first, only the money was holy, and פדיון makes the animal fully חולין (except בכור and מעשר). If the הקדש came first, the body itself was holy, and the animal keeps that holiness even after פדיון.

phrases.english: And their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption,
phrases.notes: This means young that were conceived before the redemption.

phrases.english: and one who slaughters them outside is liable,
and they make a substitute,
and if they died, they must be buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second case by reversing each law from Step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the הקדש came first, the young and milk are forbidden after פדיון, שחיטת חוץ brings liability, the animal creates a תמורה, and if it died it must be buried.

steps.title: Before redemption, the animal is exempt from firstborn and gifts
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'once redeemed,' the גמרא infers that before פדיון the animal is exempt from בכורה and מתנות. This shows the תנא holds that קדושת דמים pushes these obligations away.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The reason they owe בכורה and מתנות is that they were redeemed. So if they were not redeemed, they are exempt from בכורה and מתנות. This shows the תנא holds that holiness of value (קדושת דמים) pushes the animal out of בכורה and מתנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It reads the words 'after they were redeemed' carefully and draws out what is true before redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says these animals owe בכורה and מתנות after פדיון. So before פדיון they must be exempt. That is surprising, because an animal with a מום from the start has only קדושת דמים, not real bodily holiness. The גמרא concludes that even this lighter holiness is enough to exempt it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is X; so without X...'. A way of reading a rule from what the משנה leaves unsaid.
Holiness of value only. The animal is holy just for the money it is worth, not in its body.
Pushes away, meaning it makes the animal exempt.
He holds, meaning this is the view of the תנא.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even the weaker holiness of value is strong enough to cancel the duties of בכורה and מתנות.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The reason is that they were redeemed
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 1: animals that had a lasting מום before they were made holy.

phrases.english: but if they were not redeemed
they are exempt from firstborn status and from the gifts
phrases.notes: The 'gifts' are the parts of the animal given to a כהן.

phrases.english: He holds
holiness of value pushes away
from firstborn status and from the gifts

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the first case of the משנה, which was laid out in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before פדיון, an animal with only קדושת דמים is exempt from בכורה and מתנות.

steps.title: Shearing and work forbidden before redemption: support for רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the animals become חולין for shearing and work once redeemed. So before פדיון shearing and work are forbidden. The גמרא suggests this supports רבי אליעזר, who forbids shearing and work for קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And they go out to be חולין', and so on. The reason is that they were redeemed. So if they were not redeemed, shearing and work are forbidden. Does this support רבי אליעזר, who says animals given to בדק הבית are forbidden for shearing and work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of inference on the next phrase of the משנה. Then it suggests this backs up the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before פדיון, these animals have only קדושת דמים, just like animals given to בדק הבית. If shearing and work are forbidden here, then perhaps they are forbidden for בדק הבית animals too. That is exactly רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing the wool.
Working the animal, such as plowing.
This supports him.
Things given to the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח.

phrases.english: "And they go out to non-holy status," and so on
The reason is that they were redeemed
but if they were not redeemed
they are forbidden for shearing and work
This supports Rabbi Eliezer
who said: things consecrated for Temple upkeep
are forbidden for shearing and work?
phrases.notes: Both kinds of animal are holy only for their value. That shared point is why the משנה might back him up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reading method as step 5 on the next phrase, then turns it into a proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that קדשי בדק הבית are forbidden for shearing and work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's inference that animals with קדושת דמים are forbidden for shearing and work before פדיון.

steps.title: No proof: the ban is a rabbinic decree only for animals of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Animals of the מזבח that have קדושת דמים could be confused with animals of the מזבח that have קדושת הגוף, so the רבנן forbade them. Animals of בדק הבית have no such risk, so no decree was made for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: No. It is only holiness of value for the מזבח, which can be mixed up with bodily holiness for the מזבח, that the רבנן made a decree about. But things given to בדק הבית are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It explains why the ban in the משנה does not have to reach בדק הבית animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא suggests the ban on shearing and work here may be only a גזירה of the רבנן, not a Torah law. It would exist so that people do not confuse this animal with a truly holy animal meant for the מזבח. בדק הבית animals carry no such risk, so the משנה need not say anything about them, and the proof for רבי אליעזר falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Bodily holiness, where the animal itself is holy.
Can be confused or mixed up with.
They decreed, meaning a protective rule of the רבנן.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ban on shearing and work here comes from the Torah. According to this answer, it is only a decree of the רבנן to prevent confusion.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read as describing only a decree for animals of the מזבח, made to prevent confusion. Because of that possible reading, it cannot prove anything about בדק הבית animals.

phrases.english: They said: No
it is holiness of value for the altar
which can be confused with bodily holiness for the altar
that the Rabbis made a decree about
but things consecrated for Temple upkeep — no

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רבי אליעזר suggested in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide whether רבי אליעזר is right or wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban in the משנה is a decree limited to animals of the מזבח, made because of possible confusion. It is not a general law for everything with קדושת דמים.

steps.title: Which offspring does the משנה permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the young and milk are permitted, and asks what exact case it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Their young and their milk are permitted', and so on. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about the משנה's ruling on the offspring. The next steps will test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits the young of these animals after פדיון, but does not say when the young were conceived. The גמרא wants to pin down the exact situation the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Their young and their milk.
What is the case? What exactly are we talking about?

phrases.english: "Their young and their milk are permitted," and so on
What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה, which was listed in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When were the permitted offspring conceived and born, compared to the פדיון?

steps.title: Not offspring conceived after redemption, since that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the young was conceived and born after פדיון. Then it is obviously חולין, and the משנה would not need to say it. So this cannot be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the animal became pregnant and gave birth after its redemption, that is obvious. They are חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer and throws it out right away. That case would be too obvious for the משנה to bother teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother was already חולין when the young was conceived, there is no reason to think the young could be holy. A משנה does not teach something so plain.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, meaning a suggestion that is about to be rejected.
It is obvious. That is too plain to need teaching.
Became pregnant.

phrases.english: If you say that it became pregnant
and gave birth after their redemption
it is obvious, they are non-holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִיעַבַּר וְאִתְיְלִיד לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן — פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to the question in step 8 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as talking about young conceived after פדיון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the משנה teach something obvious.

steps.title: Offspring conceived before redemption but born after it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must mean young that was conceived while the mother was still holy, but born after her פדיון. Even that young is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where she became pregnant before the redemption and gave birth after the redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer. The משנה is talking about young conceived before פדיון and born after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is the real news. Even though the young began while its mother was holy, it comes out permitted because it was born after she was redeemed. That gives the משנה something worth teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This brings in the correct answer.
Their redemption, meaning when they are bought out of their holy status.

steps.whatToRemember: In the first case of the משנה, young conceived before פדיון but born after it is permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, where it became pregnant before their redemption
and gave birth after their redemption

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer to step 8, after the first answer was rejected in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means young conceived before פדיון and born after it.

steps.title: Young born before redemption are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's ruling, the גמרא infers that young born before the mother's פדיון are אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies: if they were born before the mother's פדיון, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and draws out what it implies for the opposite case. This short inference sets up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed that the משנה permits young conceived during קדושה but born after פדיון. If birth after פדיון is what makes the young permitted, then young born before פדיון must still be forbidden. The time of birth, not the time of conception, decides the status here.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies / but then (introduces an inference from the opposite case)
Before their redemption
They are forbidden
The young (offspring) of the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up conception and birth. The young in step 10 were also conceived while the mother was holy. The only difference here is that these were born before the פדיון.

phrases.english: But if before their redemption,
phrases.notes: He means young that were born before the mother was redeemed. This is the opposite of the case in step 10.

phrases.english: they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the opposite inference from step 10's explanation of the משנה. Young born after פדיון are permitted, so young born before פדיון are forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young of a קדשים animal born before the mother's פדיון are forbidden.
